speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of the finger being caught and pulled forcefully, this sounds like a significant traumatic injury. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and is the finger visibly deformed or misaligned compared to your other hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger.

Based on your inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger resting in extension after trauma, this is consistent with an extensor tendon avulsion. I will request an X-ray to rule out an associated fracture before we finalize the plan.

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
